Hi Samir / Elena —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Use case: server-side document enrichment + embeddings and a short real-time reranker for search.
- Traffic profile: spiky daytime traffic, ~250 req/min peak, median prompt length ~150 tokens.
- Compliance: data residency in US, strict rotation/rotation audit requirements.

Auth options we discussed (please pick preferred):
1) API keys (simple, per-service key, rotate regularly)
2) Service accounts + JWT (recommended for server-to-server, integrates w/ KMS/HSM)
3) OAuth client-credentials (if you need per-user delegations later)

Ask: can you confirm which option you prefer for the initial rollout? Also please share the procurement contact so we can loop them in for SLAs/contracting.

I've attached a short integration architecture (acme-integration-arch.pdf) and an auth comparison spreadsheet (redwood-auth-matrix.xlsx). Marissa has dropped a sample service-account JSON and minimal SDK snippet in the attachments as well.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You confirm auth approach (APIs keys vs service account vs OAuth) — due Tue 11/24
- Technical deep-dive: 60m with engineering to map routing, embeddings sizing, and key rotation strategy — propose Mon/Tue next week
- Share procurement contact (so we can provision quote/term draft)

Thanks — happy to adjust based on what you need.

Best,

Samir / Elena —

Thanks — +1 on service accounts for the initial rollout. A few engineering notes to prepare for the deep-dive:

- Architecture pattern: use short-lived JWTs minted by a Redwood service-account keypair. Store the private key in your KMS (BYOK) or we can provision a key and create a cross-account KMS grant for audit.
- Rotation approach: rotate the service-account signing key monthly. We recommend a 3-key overlapping window: active, warming, retiring — this allows zero-downtime rotation.
- SDK setup: our server SDK supports automatic key rotation hooks (see sample snippet in sample-service-account.json.txt). You can also use our OAuth client-credentials flow if you later need per-user scoping.
- Routing: for cost/latency, route inference requests to US-west for interactive traffic and US-east reserved for heavy batched embedding jobs. We can tag requests with service_account_id to enforce model/route policies.
- Embeddings/reranker: recommend starting with the redwood-embed-large model for embeddings and using a light-weight reranker in front of the expensive ranker. We'll include a staging recipe for evals.

Attachments here include: sample-service-account.json.txt (example JWT payload and RBAC claims), and a short checklist we use in Dedicated/Private deployments.

For the deep-dive, I can cover "KMS integration options" and "rotation mechanics" — would you like a short 10-slide deck to run through during the call?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
